advisory.finding: `_check_powershell_colon_interpolation` matches `$name:` anywhere in the raw action-file text, but PowerShell only treats `$name:` as a scoped-variable reference inside interpolated (double-quoted) strings and bare expressions — occurrences inside single-quoted PowerShell strings (literal, no interpolation) or unrelated YAML text will be flagged as false positives, blocking CI on a non-bug.
scenarios: A future maintainer writes a literal single-quoted PowerShell string containing `$foo:` (safe in PowerShell) and the guard rejects it as a hazard.

evidence: The pattern flags any `$name:` whose lowercased name is not in this set (scripts/check_uv_pin.py:291)
advisory.finding: The excluded-scope set is a fixed allow-list of PowerShell variable scopes and omits legitimate PSDrive/namespace qualifiers (e.g. `Function:`, `Alias:`, `HKLM:`, `Cert:`, `Variable:` is present but drive qualifiers are not), so a valid `$x` followed by a drive-qualified path or such qualifier could be spuriously reported.
scenarios: Action script legitimately references a drive/namespace-qualified path after a variable and the guard emits a false finding.
